dangerous_cpts.main_problem: This CPT has the strongest independent evidence of contributing to repeated failures. The same parameter was activated in 5 failure scenarios and 0 success scenarios, and it appears in the only reported common failure activation pattern. Semantically, the activated column corresponds to Program_Anomaly=No, Deviation_in_Response=No, Deviation_in_Dispatch=No, yet the CPT still deterministically selects Execution_Integrity=Compromised with probability 0.6. In domain terms, inferring compromised execution when all three direct indicators are absent is structurally suspicious and can directly distort downstream root-cause diagnosis.

suspicious_parameters.justification: Column 7 corresponds to Program_Anomaly=No, Deviation_in_Response=No, Deviation_in_Dispatch=No. Despite the absence of all direct execution-compromise indicators, the CPT favors Compromised over Normal. This is repeatedly associated only with failures, not successes, so the probability of Compromised in this column is likely too high.

overall_summary: Execution_Integrity is the only CPT with strong independent support for refinement. Its suspicious parameter is repeatedly and exclusively activated in failures and is semantically inconsistent with the absence of all three parent anomalies. The other candidates are weaker: Program_Anomaly may simply reflect upstream evidence absence rather than a flawed CPT, Network_Manipulation has mixed failure/success activation, and Root_Causes appears more likely to inherit upstream misclassification from Execution_Integrity than to show independent modeling error.
